name: Design Patterns Vocabulary
description: Controlled vocabulary for the Gang of Four design patterns and core API design patterns.

terms.definition: A reusable solution to a commonly occurring problem within a given context in software design.
Pattern category concerned with object creation mechanisms.
Pattern category concerned with class and object composition.
Pattern category concerned with communication between objects.
Defines an interface for creating an object but lets subclasses decide which class to instantiate.
Provides an interface for creating families of related or dependent objects.
Separates construction of a complex object from its representation.
Creates new objects by copying an existing instance.
Ensures a class has only one instance and provides a global point of access to it.
Converts the interface of a class into another interface clients expect.
Decouples an abstraction from its implementation so the two can vary independently.
Composes objects into tree structures to represent part-whole hierarchies.
Attaches additional responsibilities to an object dynamically.
Provides a unified interface to a set of interfaces in a subsystem.
Uses sharing to support large numbers of fine-grained objects efficiently.
Provides a surrogate or placeholder for another object to control access to it.
Passes a request along a chain of handlers until one handles it.
Encapsulates a request as an object, allowing parameterization, queueing, and undo.
Provides a way to access elements of a collection sequentially without exposing its representation.
Defines an object that encapsulates how a set of objects interact.
Captures an object's internal state so it can be restored later.
Defines a one-to-many dependency so observers are notified when the subject changes.
Allows an object to alter its behavior when its internal state changes.
Defines a family of algorithms, encapsulates each one, and makes them interchangeable.
Defines the skeleton of an algorithm, deferring some steps to subclasses.
Represents an operation to be performed on the elements of an object structure.
API design constraint where responses include links that drive client navigation.
Client-supplied identifier letting an API safely deduplicate retried requests.
API design pattern where the server delivers events by HTTP request to a consumer-supplied URL.
Pattern for managing long-running distributed transactions through compensating actions.
